why:
issue 1385. Hands the primary session the runtime wake callback, so an arrival the BACKEND signals — from a worker thread or an ISR, rather than from the recv the executor is parked in — cuts a parked `spin_once` short instead of letting it spend the caller's whole budget. Measured against the recorded upstream surfaces (`docs/reference/api-surface/{rclc,rclcpp,rclrs}.json`): none of them contains `wake_signal` or `set_wake_callback` at all. Upstream has no name for it because upstream has `rcl_wait` — a wait set over fds it owns — where we have one blocking session and a vtable slot a backend fills; see `c:wake_state_t` for the entity-level half of the same shape.

`pub` rather than private, which is the whole of what this row records: the three `Executor::open*` paths call it themselves, and a binding that builds its executor over a session it BORROWS (`from_session_ptr_in`) reaches none of them, so it has to call it. `rclc_executor_init` is that binding and until 1385 it did not, leaving `has_async_wake` false for the life of every C executor on every backend. Same reason `rust:Executor::set_node_identity` and `set_primary_identity` are public.

One-way: the matching clear is the executor's own (`clear_wake_signal`, run from `close()` and from `drop`), so a caller that installs owes nothing further and cannot get the teardown order wrong.
